A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, with matching title, authors, and methodological foundations. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original SAE taxonomy evaluations, GSM8K and MATH500 experiments, steering ablations, and additional appendix results.

after.justification: v4 reports original experiments across nine model pairs, including benchmark results, training-loss analyses, ablations, human validation, and SAE stability experiments.

M1.justification: v1 trains category vectors from selected sentence completions, includes a general bias vector, and searches steering coefficients/windows using thinking-model perplexity. v4 instead jointly trains category vectors and a coefficient-predicting MLP on token-disagreement positions with category-balanced cross-entropy, then uses disagreement gating and predicted coefficients during generation. These substantially change training and inference, beyond the new constructive-model-diffing terminology.

E1.justification: Category-vector training changes from MMLU-Pro reasoning traces to a mixture of MATH, Natural Reasoning, SciBench, and TheoremQA, substantially revising the represented training problems and sources. MMLU-Pro remains the taxonomy-discovery corpus. GSM8K and MATH500 remain evaluation tasks; the additional Hendrycks-MATH holdout expands sampling within existing mathematical coverage rather than establishing a new domain.

E2.justification: v4 adds four Open-Reasoner-Zero thinking models and their base counterparts to the reported base/hybrid/thinking comparisons while retaining the DeepSeek-R1-Distill and QwQ comparisons. The ablation comparator set also changes: Only-bias disappears, MLP-magnitude-only and random-position controls are added, and random-category and random-vector controls are retained with revised implementations.

E3.justification: Base/hybrid prompting explicitly changes from step-by-step chain-of-thought instructions to a minimal question–answer prompt. v4 adds a disjoint 1,000-question Hendrycks-MATH evaluation and validation-based checkpoint/run selection. Vector-training budgets and batch sizes change, and the selected R1-Qwen-1.5B taxonomy changes from 25 features to 15. These are substantive protocol revisions, not merely newly disclosed settings.

E4.justification: v4 adds training-loss comparisons, a five-seed SAE stability analysis, and human validation covering benchmark judges, taxonomy judges, and category labels. It replaces the QwQ-only MATH500 ablations with four controls on two ORZ sizes across two benchmarks. The qualitative steering example changes, and v1's narrower-sweep sensitivity results in Appendix C.3 are removed.

E5.justification: v1 already reports five taxonomy-title repetitions but gives point benchmark accuracies. v4 reports three thinking-model rollouts, three judge repetitions per rollout, and accuracy mean ± standard deviation; it also reports three independent vector-training fits, five SAE seeds, and dispersion in steering usage. Benchmark error bars describe rollout/judge variability, not variability across vector-training seeds, since one fit is selected.

E6.justification: Results are extensively replaced and expanded. For example, the Qwen2.5-32B/QwQ-32B hybrid has 84.4% MATH500 accuracy and 91% recovery in v1 Table 2, versus 66.3% and 14.3% in v4 Table 1. These use revised methods and settings and are not a controlled performance decline. New ORZ results, loss curves, human-agreement findings, and stability results support a substantially different empirical picture.

T1.justification: The SAE equations and taxonomy-score definitions are substantially retained. The limited formal revision removes v1 Appendix C.1's activation-difference expression for a steering vector and introduces v4 Appendix E.2's category-vector matrix and nonnegative state-dependent intervention alpha(h_p, c) times V_c. Neither version provides theoretical guarantees or proofs; constructive model diffing is primarily an empirical framework.

C1.justification: v1 broadly argues that reasoning mechanisms already exist in base models and that post-training, including distillation, chiefly teaches when to deploy them. v4 makes a training-paradigm distinction central: RL primarily teaches orchestration, whereas SFT-distillation introduces or modifies mechanisms. It also elevates constructive model diffing into an explicit principal contribution.

C2.justification: v4 develops a new explanation based on RL using the model's existing mechanisms versus SFT imitating potentially incompatible teacher mechanisms, with model scale affecting recoverability. It classifies QwQ as mixed SFT+RL rather than v1's RL contrast. New limitations address mathematical bias in taxonomies, thinking-model influence through the coefficient MLP, and optimization failure as an alternative explanation for low SFT recovery.

D1.justification: v4 documents training-mixture counts and exclusions, rollout generation settings, the MLP architecture, category-balanced loss, optimizer settings, checkpoint selection, and family-specific prompt templates. It also specifies benchmark decoding and grading practices that v1 leaves unclear. The cited code-access path changes from cot-interp to thinking-llms-interp. These substantially expand and revise the reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v4 substantially repositions the work relative to model diffing and crosscoders, adding discussion of Lindsey et al. and Minder et al. It also adds SAE-stability research, rank-1 LoRA findings, and concurrent steering approaches by Cheng et al. and Zhang et al. The earlier direct-base-steering novelty claim gives way to explicit distinctions based on constructive diffing and training-paradigm diagnosis.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Section 3 is reorganized around motivation, framework, training, heuristics, and evaluation; taxonomy exposition is restructured, related work gains thematic subdivisions, and a dedicated Discussion & Limitations section appears. Appendices are reorganized and expanded, while the earlier contents listing and standalone reproducibility statement disappear.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout. Separate benchmark tables are consolidated into a grouped three-benchmark table; the taxonomy heatmap is redesigned and expanded; training-loss and ablation plots are added; and the qualitative example is replaced. Appendix taxonomy tables gain full description columns, while steering-usage prose becomes structured tables.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially strengthens the investigation by directly comparing four RL-trained pairs with distilled and mixed models, replacing v1's broad post-training interpretation with a more differentiated account. Human validation addresses v1's explicitly unvalidated judges, while seed-stability tests, stronger component controls, and detailed implementation information improve credibility and reproducibility. Important limits remain: taxonomy-judge agreement is moderate overall, and low SFT recovery may reflect optimization limitations. Changed protocols also prevent interpreting the revised scores as controlled performance gains or losses. These qualifications do not outweigh the substantial evidential improvements.
